Dorian Mode on Guitar: D Dorian in 3 Positions, String by String

D Dorian contains D E F G A B C. Begin at frets 0–3 with open strings, then try the positions around the roots at fret 5 on string 5 and fret 10 on string 6.

Notes and degrees

NoteDegreeSemitones from root
DR (root)0
E2 (major 2nd)2
Fm3 (minor 3rd)3
G4 (perfect 4th)5
A5 (perfect 5th)7
B6 (major 6th)9
Cm7 (minor 7th)10

D Dorian uses the same seven notes as C major, counted from D instead of C. This changes the root and the degrees. Unlike natural minor, Dorian has a major 6th.

Full fretboard

Each circle shows a degree, with its note name below. Roots are labeled R and highlighted in amber. Fret 0 is an open string.

Frequently asked questions

Does D Dorian use different notes from C major?
No. They share the same seven notes. Counting from D gives the Dorian degrees.
How does Dorian differ from natural minor?
Dorian is a minor scale with a major 6th.
Which chord can I play it over?
Choose D Dorian over Dm7.
